chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, who said: Abdul-Adheem ibn Abdillah (who was ill) narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Umar from Hamad ibn Uthman from Isa ibn al-Sarri al-Yusri, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever dies without recognizing his Imam, dies a death of ignorance (Jahiliyyah).'
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'You will be most in need of it (recognition of the Imam) when the soul reaches here,' and he pointed with his hand to his chest.
He said: 'Indeed, I was upon a good matter (or state of affairs).'

key_terms.أَبِی عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.إِمَامُ: Imam, the divinely appointed leader and guide
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: The Messenger of Allah, referring to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family)
key_terms.مِیتَهً جَاهِلِیَّهً: Death of ignorance, a state of spiritual loss akin to pre-Islamic times

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of dying without recognizing the Imam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (a) clarifies that the 'recognition' (Ma'rifah) of the Imam is not merely intellectual but a spiritual anchor, becoming most critical at the moment of death when the soul departs the body. By pointing to his chest, the Imam emphasizes that this recognition must reside in the heart, ensuring the believer dies in a state of spiritual continuity with the divine authority. This hadith underscores the Shia doctrine that Ma'rifah al-Imam is the key to salvation, linking the temporal authority of the Imams to the eternal fate of the soul.
